issues.what: The full-design logistic learner (online/full/logts, 108 of 468 rows per timeframe, 'outside the frozen shortlist') is a degenerate fit, not a working learner: the Laplace/Newton logistic on ~305 online-standardised columns with prior precision 1.0 saturates, so p_model is exactly 0 or 1 on 99.7% (minute) / 98.9% (5minute) of SETUPs for k=1 and 99.3% / 92.7% for k=10/300. Consequently the decisions are bit-identical across window (anchored = 300 = 1000), across the net / pf decision heads (W vs 1.5 L is irrelevant when p is 0/1) and across all five Thompson seeds (chol(H^-1) ~ I and |x.w| >> 35): 36 ledger rows share (kept_n 2241, diff 11.08, PF 0.315) on minute, 36 share (428, -477.93, 0.538) on 5minute. FINDINGS prints the seed-spread rows with 'diff sd 0.00' and the family line 'full logts 108 paths, diff > 0 in 108' and puts full/logts rows through the finalist go/no-go (ee3bb53f8c7251b8, 4d0b2708b7798f80) without saying the learner diverged. The 'two linear learners on the full design as a labelled sensitivity' was therefore only performed for lints; the logts sensitivity is untested, not null. This does not change the verdict (no candidate, 0 row-level passes) and the context-design logts is healthy (p_model 0.10-0.21 / 0.18-0.44), so it is a reporting gap, not a false claim of a survivor.

issues.fix: Add a caveat to FINDINGS.md / findings.json: 'online/full/logts diverged (p saturated 0/1 on >= 93% of rows); its 108 rows per timeframe are ~6 distinct decision vectors and are not evidence about a logistic learner on the full design'. If the sensitivity is wanted, re-run only full/logts with a stronger prior (precision ~ d or chosen by nested evidence) or a step-halved Newton, as new ledger rows counted in the family; do not present the existing rows as a learner outcome.

issues.what: The kept books of the top rows mix the 30 warm-up take-all trades (common to every path; mean -802 INR on minute, -543 on 5minute) with the learner's own takes, and FINDINGS never separates them. The best minute row 19f7ff81224bafa0 (kept 68, PF 1.077) is 30 warm-up trades (sum -24,061) plus 38 learned takes (mean +834, PF 1.495, last take 2022-11-04); the best 5minute row e24ac736ebbfa6d5 (kept 140, PF 0.942) is 30 warm-up plus 110 learned takes (mean +9, PF 1.005, last take 2023-11-06). Every context finalist stops taking anything after 1-2 years, which the learning-curve tables show (kept n flat) but the text does not name. No number is wrong and the row-level floors fail either way; this is an omission that affects how the 'best PF' rows should be read.
